G2424: Jesus (ישוע): The name given to the Messiah, derived from the Hebrew root meaning 'to save.' See Strong G2424.
G3056: Logos (λόγος): Word, discourse, reason. The divine principle of revelation and communication, particularly applied to Christ in John 1:1.
G2316: Theos (θεός): God, the supreme divine being, source of all existence and moral authority.
G26: Agape (ἀγάπη): Self-sacrificial, unconditional love — the highest form of love in Christian theology, shown by God's love for humanity.
G4102: Pistis (πίστς): Faith, trust, conviction; the faculty of believing in something — especially trust in God or Christ for salvation.
G5485: Charis (χάρις): Grace, favor, kindness — unmerited divine favor and love given freely by God, not earned.
G4151: Pneuma (πνεῦμα): Spirit, breath, wind; the Holy Spirit as the third person of the Trinity, or human spirit.
G932: Basileia (βασιλεία): Kingdom, reign, sovereignty — the realm or domain of a king, particularly the Kingdom of God/Heaven.
G2098: Euaggelion (εὐαγγέλιον): Gospel, good news — the message of salvation through Christ, or the four Gospel books.
G1577: Ekklesia (ἐκκλησία): Church, assembly — the called-out people of God, the body of Christ, gathered for worship and fellowship.
G2588: Kardia (καρδία): Heart — the inner being, seat of emotions, will, and intellect; the mind's center in Hebrew/Greek thought.
G756: Arche (ἀρχή): Beginning, origin, first principle — the original source or ruler; used in Genesis 1:1 and John 1:1.
G1108: Gnosis (γνῶσις): Knowledge, understanding — especially spiritual or theological knowledge gained through experience.
G1242: Diatheke (διαθήκη): Covenant, testament — a binding agreement or arrangement, particularly the New Covenant in Christ's blood.
G1343: Dikaiosyne (δικαιοσύνη): Righteousness, justice — the quality of being right, moral uprightness, and conformity to God's will.
G3144: Martys (μάρτυς): Witness, martyr — one who testifies to or bears evidence of something, often at the cost of life.
G3341: Metanoia (μετάνοια): Repentance — a change of mind, turning from sin, conversion, a fundamental shift in thinking and direction.
G5046: Teleios (τέλειος): Perfect, complete, mature — having reached its intended end, fully developed and without deficiency.
G4095: Pino (πίνω): To drink — literal or figurative consumption, especially of spiritual nourishment.
G1110: Ginomai (γίνομαι): To become, come into being, happen — describing origin or transformation of a person or thing.
G1510: Eimi (εἰμί): To be, exist — the fundamental verb of being; foundational to Greek metaphysics and theology.
G2036: Ero (ἔπον): To say, speak — used in proclamation, instruction, or declarative speech.
G3584: O (ὅς): Who, which, that — a relative pronoun introducing clauses or phrases.
H430: Elohim (אֱלֹהִים): Gods, deity — a plural noun applied to the one true God, emphasizing power and majesty.
H3068: Yahweh (יְהֹוָה): The eternal, self-existent God of Israel — the divine name revealed to Moses, unchanging and supreme.
H1254: Bara (בָּרָא): To create, shape, form — specifically divine creation from nothing, reserved for God's acts alone.
H7225: Reshith (רֵאשִׁית): Beginning, first, chief — the origin or foremost part of something; head of an enterprise.
H8064: Shamayim (שָׁמַיִם): Heavens, sky — the celestial realm, abode of God and angels, stretching above the earth.
H776: Erets (אֶרֶץ): Earth, land, ground — the physical world, often referring to the inhabited earth or specific territories.
H7965: Shalom (שָׁלוֹם): Peace, wholeness, well-being — completeness in every area of life, not merely absence of conflict.
H1285: Berith (בְּרִית): Covenant, treaty — a solemn, binding agreement between two parties, especially God and Israel.
H3820: Leb (לֵב): Heart, mind — the inner self; seat of thought, emotion, will, and understanding.
H1818: Dam (דָּם): Blood — life force, atonement, or sacrificial offering; central to Hebrew ritual and theology.
H2617: Chesed (חֶסֶד): Covenant love, mercy, steadfast kindness — God's loyal, unfailing love toward His people.
H5030: Nabi (נָבִיא): Prophet — one who speaks for God, revealing divine will, often foretelling future events.
H8451: Torah (תּוֹרָה): Law, instruction, teaching — divine guidance for living; the first five books of the Bible or their teachings.
